question: did the timber re-tone change what the shipped viewer draws, and can this frame judge it
method: same page, same walk station, same camera, before and after the re-tone; the wall and floor act as a control because nothing about them changed
findings: The re-tone is live and behaves as designed: the controls are byte-identical, and the timber moves in exactly the channels the gain touches - red most, green a little, blue not at all (gain 2.34, 1.41, 0.98).

This frame cannot judge the timber colour. The door face in it sits at sRGB 15 against a wall at 160, a tenfold difference: it is the back of an open door turned into a dark corner, and almost nothing of what it shows is diffuse. A 2.34x lift in albedo moved it two levels.

So the black door in the pre-re-tone frame was shade, not albedo, and the re-tone should not be credited with fixing it. The re-tone stands on the hue measurement in build/timber-colour-r41.json alone - the delivery sat at red/blue 2.09 where both estimates of the photographs put it past 3.3 - and that basis is unaffected by any of this.
outstanding: a frame with a lit door face. The turn frames from the same run sweep the view and may catch one; failing that, a walk station in a room whose door faces a window.
